hints.title: Reference Unit Normalization
hints.text: Calculate the conversion ratio of every unit with respect to base unit 0 using modular multiplication.

hints.title: Modular Multiplicative Inverse
hints.text: The ratio between unit u and unit v is value[v] multiplied by the modular inverse of value[u].

hints.title: Fermat Little Theorem
hints.text: For prime modulus p = 10^9 + 7, compute inverse using pow(val, p - 2, p).

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import deque

class Solution:
    def queryConversions(self, conversions: list[list[int]], queries: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        n = len(conversions) + 1
        units = [0] * n
        units[0] = 1
        graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v, factor in conversions:
            graph[u].append((v, factor))
        q = deque([0])
        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            for v, factor in graph[u]:
                units[v] = (units[u] * factor) % MOD
                q.append(v)

        ans = []
        for u, v in queries:
            ans.append((units[v] * pow(units[u], MOD - 2, MOD)) % MOD)
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Breadth-first traversal precomputes absolute ratios, and queries evaluate using modular inverses.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Running graph traversals from source node u for each query takes O(Q * N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Linear storage of base ratios accelerates query resolution.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use root-normalized values with modular inverses for constant-time conversion queries.
